$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 11 of N, 2026-11-24 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.referenceDefinition.multiple: A field such as a product's categories points at many records and not one; the flag makes the field hold a list of references, so a many-to-many link is declared on the field and not by hand-building a join concept.
reasons.panelLayout.type: A panel can be a table of rows, a grid, a console or a dashboard of widgets, with the table as the default; the type picks which, so one panel declaration changes shape without a separate screen technology.
reasons.flowStep.args: A step that calls a capability, such as sending an email, passes values in; the arguments are positional, each a literal or a reference to flow state, so the call states its inputs in order and needs no glue code.
reasons.query.groupBy: A report such as sales per month per region groups rows; the group-by fields, plain fields, date buckets or reference paths, make the query an aggregate query, so totals come from the query and not from loading every row and adding them up in a flow.
reasons.schemaObject.minLength: A code or a name must not be empty or too short; the minimum length of a text is checked at the boundary for every caller, so a short value is refused before any rule sees it.
reasons.pack:requires: A pack that takes payments needs a role or an outbound network address that the app must supply; requires lists the roles, capabilities and network access the pack needs and composition refuses when one is unbound, so an install fails clearly and not at runtime.
reasons.guidePage.regions: A guide page may show areas around its gadgets, such as a side menu; the regions block holds the settings of those areas together, so each page shows only the areas it needs.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.labelField: A generated selection or prompt must show a row as readable text, such as a customer's name and not its id; the label field names the field used for that text, so lookups read well without a hand-declared panel.
reasons.enumOption.description: A choice such as a ticket priority may need a sentence saying what each member means; the description carries it for help text and screens, so the meaning travels with the value and not in a separate document.
reasons.flowStep.value: A flow's answer or an intermediate result is computed from the flow's state; value gives it, as the answer of a return step or the expression whose result a set step stores, so small calculations need no function and no code.
reasons.pack:$schema: An editor can offer completion and spot mistakes in a pack file when it knows the schema; this optional address tells it which one and has no effect on the pack.
reasons.presentationMetadata.visibleWhen: A field that matters only in some cases, such as a reason for rejection, should appear only then; an expression over the record shows the control while it is true, so the form adapts without a custom screen script.
reasons.workbenchAction.procedure: A workbench button, such as pricing the draft, needs something to run; the named flow is invoked over the draft, and it cannot be combined with checkBalances, so the rule lives in a flow that other callers can reuse and the button holds no logic.
